title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Furman spaces for group work, quiet study, campus events, art, reflection, and everyday student meetups.

cards.title: Meet Without Booking a Formal Room
cards.subtitle: Commons overlooking Furman Lake
cards.notes: Swipe into the commons, choose seating near the lake view, and use this as a flexible meetup point for studying or conversation.
cards.short_summary: A round-the-clock student commons connecting social, academic, and campus-life resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman describes Trone as a place for students to meet, eat, socialize, and study; students may access its commons 24/7 by swiping a student ID.
cards.access_notes: Commons access is 24/7 for students using a Furman ID; individual businesses and offices keep separate posted hours.

cards.entity_name: James B. Duke Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Give a Group Project Its Own Room
cards.subtitle: Lower level and first floor of Duke Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room through the library site when your group needs conversation space, a shared table, and fewer interruptions.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms designed for collaborative assignments and study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s current study-space inventory identifies group study rooms on Duke Library’s lower level and first floor, with rooms reservable through the library website.
cards.access_notes: Room availability and reservation rules are controlled through the university library; follow current library building hours.

cards.title: Use a Computer Without Hunting Across Campus
cards.subtitle: Main level of James B. Duke Library
cards.notes: Head to the main-level Research Commons when an assignment needs a campus computer alongside library research resources.
cards.short_summary: A named library workspace with a substantial bank of student computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman Information Technology Services lists the Duke Library Research Commons on the library’s main level with 33 Windows computers.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Information Technology Services | Furman University
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Duke Library access hours and Furman’s current computer-lab policies.

cards.title: Read Between the Room’s Hosted Events
cards.subtitle: An Asian Studies space inside Furman Hall
cards.notes: Check whether an event is scheduled, then use the open reading room for a quieter change of setting inside Furman Hall.
cards.short_summary: An event-capable reading room that reopens to students between scheduled programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s Asian Studies department says the James B. Leavell Reading Room hosts receptions, open houses, and student events and is open to students when no event is underway.
cards.source_title: Facilities & Resources | Asian Studies | Furman University
cards.access_notes: Student access is available when the room is not hosting an event; confirm building access and posted scheduling.

cards.title: Switch Between Quiet Work and Conversation
cards.subtitle: First floor of Furman Hall
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing to the first-floor lounge, where the department documents space for quiet study and faculty conversation.
cards.short_summary: A departmental lounge serving both focused work and informal academic exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman’s English department describes its first-floor lounge as a quiet study spot, a place to speak with faculty over coffee or tea, and a venue for class activities.
cards.access_notes: Use during normal Furman Hall access and respect department activities or classes occupying the lounge.

cards.entity_name: Robert J. Maxwell Music Media Center & Library
cards.title: Work With Scores, Recordings, and Audio Tools
cards.subtitle: Music research space in Herring Music Pavilion
cards.notes: Use the music library, listening lab, or digital workstation when coursework calls for focused listening or recording research.
cards.short_summary: A specialized music workspace combining collections, listening facilities, and digital production tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman identifies the Maxwell Music Media Center and Library as an in-building research library with a listening lab, reference center, and digital workstation and recording booth.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and equipment use may follow Music Department or library rules; verify current hours before visiting.

cards.title: See What the Art Building Is Working On
cards.subtitle: Contemporary exhibitions inside Roe Art Building
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition calendar, then stop between classes to view work presented during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A rotating campus gallery where exhibitions connect students with contemporary creative practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman states that Thompson Art Gallery is located in the Thomas Anderson Roe Art Building and presents rotating contemporary artwork during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Thompson Art Gallery and Department Events Schedule | Furman University
cards.access_notes: Visit only during posted gallery hours or scheduled programs; confirm the current exhibition calendar before going.

cards.title: Use the Lower Level for Student Gatherings
cards.subtitle: Meeting rooms and common space across from Duke Library
cards.notes: Coordinate with Spiritual Life before bringing a group downstairs for discussion, dinner, study, or a religious meeting.
cards.short_summary: The chapel’s lower level supports student-led meetings beyond services in the sanctuary.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman says students use Daniel Chapel’s downstairs space for religious-group meetings, while its lower-level meeting rooms and commons support discussions and weekly dinners.
cards.source_title: History & Architecture | Daniel Chapel | Furman University
cards.access_notes: Contact Spiritual Life about reserving lower-level space; worship, performances, and other scheduled events take priority.

cards.title: Take a Deliberate Walk Between Commitments
cards.subtitle: Brick walking path on the chapel lawn
cards.notes: Follow the brick path at your own pace when you want a structured pause for thought, meditation, prayer, or reflection.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor contemplative path built for walking, stillness, and focused thought.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman identifies the chapel lawn’s brick labyrinth as a meditative tool and documents people walking, sitting, meditating, praying, and seeking guidance there.
cards.source_title: Labyrinth | Office of Spiritual Life | Furman University
cards.access_notes: The university describes the outdoor labyrinth as open all day, every day; use it respectfully and yield to organized activities.

cards.title: Slow Down at the Lake’s Japanese Temple
cards.subtitle: Contemplative space beside the Asia Garden
cards.notes: Walk the adjoining garden or pause for reflection; visit during docent hours when you want historical context about the temple.
cards.short_summary: A reconstructed Japanese temple and garden setting used for reflection, teaching, and connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Furman invites visitors to stroll and meditate at the Place of Peace and adjoining Asia Garden; Asian Studies also uses the temple as a teaching tool and meeting space.
cards.access_notes: Public docents are listed Saturday and Sunday from 1–3 p.m.; outdoor garden access and temple entry may differ, so follow posted signs.
